title: Black Bean & Egg White Breakfast Burritos
subtitle: Vegetarian breakfast burritos built on egg whites, black beans, and pepper jack.
description: Egg whites scramble up with black beans, bell pepper, and onion, then get wrapped in a warm tortilla with pepper jack and salsa. It is a fully vegetarian, higher-protein burrito option next to the hall's usual sausage versions.

steps.title: Sauté the vegetables
steps.instruction: Heat a splash of oil in a large skillet over medium. Cook onion and bell pepper 5–6 minutes until softened.

steps.title: Warm the black beans
steps.instruction: Add black beans to the pan with the vegetables and warm through, 4–5 minutes, seasoning with a pinch of salt and cumin if desired.

steps.title: Scramble the egg whites
steps.instruction: Move beans and vegetables to one side of the pan or a separate pan. Pour in egg whites and scramble gently over medium-low until just set — they firm up fast, so don't walk away.

steps.title: Build and wrap for the line
steps.instruction: Warm tortillas briefly. Fill with egg whites, bean-vegetable mixture, cheese, and a spoon of salsa. Fold in the sides, then roll forward tightly. Hold seam-side down on a warm tray.

steps.title: Serve and hold
steps.instruction: Hold wrapped burritos in a 200°F oven, uncovered for a crisper tortilla or covered for a softer one. Serve with hot sauce on the side.

stationWorkflow: Cook vegetables and beans first since they hold well while the egg whites finish.
Scramble egg whites gently and pull them slightly underdone — they keep setting off the heat.
Wrap burritos tightly so fillings stay contained through the line.
cleanupNotes: Wipe the egg white pan while warm to prevent set residue from sticking.
Rinse the bean pan promptly — bean starch dries stubborn if left to sit.
leftovers: Wrap cooled burritos individually in foil and refrigerate up to 4 days, or freeze up to 2 months.
Reheat wrapped in foil at 350°F for 15–18 minutes, or unwrapped in a skillet for a crisper tortilla.
